newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRIMA HITS CZECH SCREENS SEEKING 15 PCT VIEWERSHIP.
newsitem.headline: PRIMA HITS CZECH SCREENS SEEKING 15 PCT VIEWERSHIP.

text.p: The reconstructed nationwide Czech commercial television station Prima, launched on Friday, hopes to capture a 15 percent share of viewers by the end of 1997, its general director said.

Prima, created from the remnants of the struggling 1994-launched Premiera TV, is looking to cut into the dominance of the country's first commercial station, TV Nova, which now controls about 65 perecent of the market.
"We would like to get more than 10 percent (of viewers) as quickly as possible, and at the end of this year we want to reach more than 15 percent," Milos Petana, Prima's director told Reuters.

Prima, with a new brighter look, graphics package, and programme lineup, must build on Premiera's lagging ratings which in the third quarter totalled only 4.2 percent of the market, accoring to a survey by research firms Median and GfK.
The station's signal penetration has grown to cover nearly two-thirds of the country's roughly four million TV households, and that is expected to rise to 75 percent by the end of 1997.
Prima's owners include licence holder FTV Premiera with a 47 percent stake.
FTV Premiera is majority owned by the Czech bank IPB a.s. , which also holds a separate 14 percent stake.

U.S.-born investor Michael Dingman's Stratton Investments Ltd holds a 15 percent stake in Prima, while Czech Kapitalova Investicni Spolecnost a.s. has 14 percent and insurer Ceska Pojistovna has 10 percent.
Petana said there should be soon major changes in the owners' structure but he declined to elaborate.
"I admit, there will be major changes in this portfolio, most probably during the first quarter of the year," he said.
Prima is starting from scratch with a new programming line-up beginning this weekend, after nearly three years of not-so-popular offerings.
Petana said Prima would be geared toward "live programmes, afternoon entertainment and competition programmes, nine or ten films a week in the evening, and ten serials at a time",
Czech media analysts expect Prima may have to adopt more of the flashy tabloid style of TV Nova if it wants to draw Nova's commercial clients.

The public broadcaster CTV lost its monopoly when Nova, controlled by Central European Media Enterprises Ltd. which was founded by New York cosmetics heir Ronald Lauder, took over a former state broadcast signal in Febraury, 1994.
Nova burst on Czech screens with a mix of mostly American serials, action films, and tabloid news programmes, and has become a profitable fixture in the country's pop culture.
Analysts estimate that total turnover in mainstream Czech advertising revenue will approach $500 million this year after grossing just over $400 million in 1995.
